answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs thus has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the echo hash is checked against the zephyr checkpoint at intake, the quartz audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 7 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
